To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the contact stiffness of elastic bodies rises much more steep with contact radius than expected from Hertzian contact theory, and that this effect is much more pronounced for nearly incompressible bodies.

the contact stiffness and the penetration of a coated material rise more steeply than those of a homogeneous material, and that the penetration increasingly deviates from a homogeneous reference case when approaching a Poisson ratio equal to 0.5.

the contact stiffness increases more rapidly with contact radius for nearly incompressible than for compressible layers, that significant elastic pile-up occurs for nearly incompressable layers and that this effect is more pronounced for softer layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the contact of a coated body with a rigid indenter.
the axisymmetric contact of a rigid indenter and a coated elastic body.
the development of a new numerical method for the frictional contact of coated bodies, and its application to the instrumented indentation test.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contact stiffness of coated materials is not a simple additive property of the two materials involved.
the contact stiffness of incompressible coatings is much more dependent upon the contact radius than for compressible coatings.
, for the case of coated bodies, the Poisson ratio of the coating material is a crucial parameter for the indentation data analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the indentation data analysis of elastic materials should not be done without considering the coating effects, especially for the materials with high Poisson ratio.
we have developed an efficient and accurate algorithm for the frictionless axisymmetric contact of elastic bodies, which is able to handle the case of nearly incompressible and/or soft materials.

the indentation response on a coated body depends strongly on the coating material properties, and it is not always possible to extract the coating properties from indentation data alone, unless the substrate properties are also known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contact stiffness of coated systems is not a simple function of the contact radius, but depends on the material properties of the coating and the underlying substrate.
the contact stiffness is a very sensitive indicator of the coating mechanical properties.
indentation of a nearly incompressible layer is much more complex than the corresponding indentation of a more compressible layer.
